method: Full pinned C implementation read; Git blob and SHA256 verified. Source review only, no new execution.
findings: State constructors zero-initialize via GLib slice allocation; copy duplicates whole state including retained tail and total length. Steal copies accumulators into locals and emits result without consuming state; finalise calls steal then frees.

Nonzero seed in each one-shot wrapper is fed as four native-order input bytes before message, rather than initializing accumulator fields. Thus conventional MurmurHash3 seeded interchange cannot be inferred from function names; no independent oracle run here.

GET_UINT32/64 use direct cast dereferences; source explicitly warns big/little endian differ and asks alignment-restricted platforms to adjust conversion. Output similarly writes integer words directly, leaving serialization host-dependent.

MURMUR_FILL_XS casts size_t input length to int in its byte-count expression. Large updates with an existing tail can narrow length or overflow signed arithmetic before memcpy. Potential failure is source-level; no giant read or copy executed.

x86_128 tail assembly shifts promoted uint8 values by24 without first converting to uint32_t. High-bit tail bytes can invoke signed-shift portability issues. x64 tail path explicitly casts to uint64_t.

x64 state-equality helper compares accumulators, lengths and only live tail bytes, avoiding irrelevant tail garbage. It does not compare underlying source bytes; hash-state equality is not independent file equality.
limits: No end-to-end scanner or portable Murmur compatibility claim.
